variants.q: A campaign's optimal 10-seed spread is 40,000 users. Given: greedy >= 0.632 x optimal. Minimum greedy spread?
Greedy reached 25,000 users. What is the most the optimal spread could be?

why.q: Why settle for an approximation instead of the optimal seed set?
why.a: Finding the optimum is NP-hard: checking every k-subset of millions of nodes is infeasible. Greedy runs in practical time with a proven 63% guarantee.

title: STL anomaly rule: flag |residual| > k x IQR of residuals
given: STL splits a series into trend, seasonal and residual, and flags residuals whose absolute value exceeds k x IQR. Example (not on slide): residual Q1 = -0.65, Q3 = 1.25, k = 3.
solution_steps: Threshold = 3 x 1.9 = 5.7.
New residuals to check (quartiles come from the agent's history): Residuals [1.2, -0.8, 0.5, 2.0, -1.5, 9.4, 0.3, -0.2]: only 9.4 has |r| > 5.7, so that hour is the anomaly.
answer: IQR 1.9, threshold 5.7; the residual 9.4 is flagged.

variants.q: bKash residuals for one agent have Q1 = -2 and Q3 = 4. Given: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 6 and k = 2. What is the flag threshold?
With that threshold (12), which residuals are flagged: 5, -14, 11, 30?

why.q: Why flag the residual and not the raw value?
why.a: The raw value includes trend and seasonality: a high Friday-evening value may be normal. Once STL removes the expected trend and season, what is left is the unexplained part, so a big residual means truly unusual behaviour. IQR is robust to the outliers it is trying to find.

title: Kwak 2010: 41.7 M users, 1.47 B edges, 22.1% reciprocity, alpha 2.276
given: 41.7 M users, 1.47 billion following edges, 106 M tweets. 77.9% of users have a follower they do not follow back; 22.1% of relationships mutual. Power law P(k) ∝ k^-2.276. Top 0.05% have >1 M followers. 85% of trending topics are news; median trend lasts 17.5 h.
solution_steps: Average out-degree = 1.47e9 / 41.7e6 = 35.25 follows per user.
Mutual relationships = 22.1% of 1.47 B = 324.87 million.
Top 0.05% of 41.7 M = 20,850 users with >1 M followers.
Power law: doubling k cuts P(k) by 2^2.276 = 4.84x.
Of 200 trending topics, 85% = 170 news, 15% = 30 memes.
answer: Average 35.3 follows per user; 20,850 celebrities; P(k) falls 4.8x when k doubles.

variants.q: A graph has 2 million users and 70 million directed edges. Given: average out-degree = edges / users. Compute it.
In that graph 22.1% of edges are reciprocated. How many mutual edges?

why.q: Why do the low reciprocity and fast trending make Twitter a 'news medium' rather than a social network?
why.a: Most following is one-way broadcasting from a few hubs to many followers (77.9% asymmetry, power-law in-degree), and 85% of trending topics are headline news peaking within 15 minutes. It behaves like a news wire, which is why it became a public-health surveillance signal.

title: Syndromic lead times: Twitter 7-10 days, pharmacy 3-5 days, CDC lag 1-2 weeks
given: Physician reports reach CDC 1-2 weeks after symptoms. Twitter posts with 'flu', 'fever', 'can't taste' peak 7-10 days before ER visits. OTC antipyretic sales spike 3-5 days before clinical confirmation. ILINet: >3,000 sentinel physicians; BioSense: 3,500+ EDs.
solution_steps: ER visits peak on 20 October.
Twitter signal peaks 7-10 days earlier: 10-13 October.
Taking 20 October as the clinical confirmation date, the pharmacy spike comes 3-5 days earlier: 15-17 October.
Traditional report reaches CDC 1-2 weeks after symptoms: 27 October to 3 November (if symptoms start 20 October).
answer: Twitter about 10-13 Oct, pharmacy 15-17 Oct, ER peak 20 Oct, CDC reports 27 Oct-3 Nov.

variants.q: Dengue ER visits in Dhaka peak on 15 September. Given: social posts peak 7-10 days before ER visits. When does the social signal peak?
Clinical confirmation is on 12 March. Given: pharmacy sales spike 3-5 days earlier. When is the spike?

why.q: Why do pharmacy sales lead clinical confirmation?
why.a: People self-medicate with paracetamol or ibuprofen as soon as symptoms start, days before they see a doctor and long before a diagnosis is reported. Sales data capture illness at that earlier stage.

slides: W10 P2 s17 (Live Exercise); W10 P2 s10, s15 (Discussion Q2)
title: Live Exercise: synthetic weekly ILI = 5 + 3 sin(2πt/52 - π/2) + noise
given: 156 weekly points (3 years). ili = 5 + 3 sin(2π t / 52 - π/2) + N(0, 0.5), clipped at 0. Fit Prophet with yearly and weekly seasonality, forecast 12 weeks, add an Eid holiday (upper_window 3), change changepoint_prior_scale 0.05 -> 0.5.
solution_steps: t = 0: 5 + 3 sin(-π/2) = 2 (trough).
Period 52 weeks = 1 year; 156 / 52 = 3 seasons.
Forecast 12 weeks beyond week 155 (weeks 156-167).
changepoint_prior_scale 0.05 -> 0.5 is 10x looser: the trend bends more easily (more flexible, risk of overfitting).
Discussion Q2: a sudden COVID wave is a trend changepoint, caught by g(t); the changepoint_prior_scale sets how readily new changepoints are accepted.
answer: Trough 2 at week 0, mean 5 at week 13, peak 8 at week 26; 3 full seasons; prior scale raised 10x.

variants.q: Same formula. Given: sin(2π·39/52 - π/2) = sin(π) = 0. What is the expected ILI at week 39?
A model's yearly Fourier seasonality uses N = 10 terms (each with a cos and a sin coefficient). How many seasonal coefficients are fitted? Add weekly with N = 3.

why.q: Why does Prophet's g + s + h structure suit epidemiologists better than a black-box model?
why.a: Each component can be inspected and adjusted on its own: trend changepoints, annual flu season, holiday effects such as Eid. Domain experts can audit and tune it without ARIMA expertise, and the additive form absorbs spikes without corrupting the trend.

title: Social and surveillance scale: YouTube 500 h/min, 500 M tweets/day, BioSense 38 M visits
given: YouTube: 500 hours uploaded per minute. Twitter/X: 500 M tweets/day. BioSense 2019-20: 38 million ED visits; Prophet ran on 60 HHS regions in parallel; 3,500+ EDs. Facebook ran Prophet on 500,000+ series.
solution_steps: YouTube per day = 500 x 60 x 24 = 720,000 hours of video.
Tweets per second = 500e6 / 86,400 = 5,787.
ED visits per ED = 38e6 / 3,500 = 10,857 per season.
500,000 Prophet series on 1,000 executors = 500 series each.
answer: 720,000 hours/day of video; about 5,787 tweets/s; about 10,857 visits per ED.

variants.q: A platform receives 100 million posts per day. Given: per second = daily / 86,400. Rate?
60 HHS regions are forecast in parallel with applyInPandas on 12 executors. How many region models per executor?

why.q: Why does the slide say social media's graph, not the individual post, is the main analytical object?
why.a: Influence, communities and cascades are properties of who follows and retweets whom. Single posts are short and noisy; the network structure explains how information spreads.

title: Vectorised Prophet: 5,000 SKUs, 8 h to about 12 min on 20 executors (40x)
given: 90-day forecasts for 5,000 store-product SKUs. Sequential Prophet on one machine: 8+ hours. Spark applyInPandas, grouped by sku_id, on a 20-executor cluster: about 12 minutes.
solution_steps: Speedup = 8 x 60 / 12 = 40x.
Models per executor = 5,000 / 20 = 250.
Sequential time per model = 480 min / 5,000 = 5.76 s.

One model at a time per executor would take 250 x 5.76 s = 24 min; the measured 12 min is half that, which implies about 2 models running at once per executor (multi-core executors; inference, not stated on the slide).
Forecast output rows = 5,000 x 90 = 450,000.
answer: 40x speedup; 250 models per executor; 450,000 forecast rows.

variants.q: A chain has 12,000 SKUs; Prophet takes 6 s per SKU on one machine. Given: sequential time = SKUs x time per model. How long sequentially?

why.q: Why is fitting thousands of Prophet models 'embarrassingly parallel'?
why.a: Each SKU's series is fitted independently with no data shared between models. Spark groups rows by sku_id, sends each group to one task, and runs Prophet inside a Pandas UDF, so all models fit at once across the cluster.

title: Trend and anomaly spikes: 10 to 10,000 per hour = 1,000x; #QurbaniEid 1,200x
given: A phrase normally appears 10 times/hour and suddenly 10,000 times/hour: trending regardless of absolute volume. #QurbaniEid showed a 1,200x spike over 6 hours with 92% positive sentiment. A bKash agent's hourly volume jumps from 10 to 10,000 transactions.
solution_steps: Spike ratio = current rate / baseline = 10,000 / 10 = 1,000x.
The rule is relative: a phrase going 1,000 to 10,000 (10x) trends less than one going 10 to 10,000.
#QurbaniEid: if the baseline was 50 per hour, 1,200x gives 60,000 per hour.
92% positive of 60,000 tweets = 55,200 positive.
answer: 1,000x spike ratio; same arithmetic flags the bKash agent for Isolation Forest review.

A hashtag has 40,000 posts in a spike; VADER marks 92% positive. How many are not positive?

why.q: Why does trend detection use the ratio to the baseline instead of the absolute count?
why.a: Big topics are always high-volume, so absolute counts would always show the same things. A ratio to each phrase's own history finds sudden change, which is what 'trending' means. (High sentiment like 92% positive also helped show the spike was organic, not coordinated.)

title: VADER compound score thresholds: > 0.05 positive, < -0.05 negative
given: VADER outputs a compound score in [-1, +1]: positive if > 0.05, negative if < -0.05, otherwise neutral. Sample scores (not on slide): 0.62, 0.04, -0.03, -0.41, 0.05.
solution_steps: 0.62: positive.
0.04: neutral.
-0.03: neutral.
-0.41: negative.
0.05: neutral.
Share positive = 1/5 = 20%. Note 0.05 itself is neutral (the rule is strictly greater).
answer: 1 positive, 3 neutral, 1 negative.

variants.q: Three tweets score 0.30, -0.06 and 0.05. Given the thresholds, classify each.
'great' scores 0.62. Name two VADER rules that would raise the score of 'GREAT!!!'.
variants.a: Capitalisation (GREAT > great) and punctuation (great!!! > great) both intensify it.

why.q: Why use VADER instead of a general-purpose sentiment model on tweets?
why.a: VADER is a lexicon-and-rule model tuned for social media: it handles capitals, exclamation marks, degree words, negation and emojis, which dominate short noisy posts. It is cheap enough to run as a Spark UDF on every tweet.
